verdicts.evidence: The timetable facts appear only in prose: "every forty minutes between early morning and late evening" in paragraph one, and "thins to one boat each hour", "before dusk" and "Printed timetables are kept in the shelter at each landing" in paragraph three, with no hours or winter dates anywhere.

The second sentence of the first paragraph runs from "Each crossing takes about twelve minutes" to "on most mornings at low tide" across five lines, and "a little longer" has no figure; it is about 42 words, not 49, but the run-on is there.
